items.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: Max Jones would review and would enthuse about everyone from Marion Williams and the Stars of Faith, right through to Duke Ellington or Charlie Parker. They were all part of a piece as far as we were concerned.

ctx.x: Is there an exotic factor to something, an art form that comes from another country?

I think all of us were kind of caught up in the racial element of it. You know a lot of the writers and a lot of the opinion formers were leftward leaning, right socialist people, and what they were empathizing with was of course the situation for black Americans, a tremendous interest in the blues, a tremendous interest in the formative experiences of black musicians, and of a sense of trying to do something to arrest or correct injustice. That was a powerful strand in the kind of reading I did and in the kind…
Did they have an interest in people like Frankie Trumbauer, Bix Beiderbecke?
